invariants.statement: CredentialBinding is separate from RuntimeProfile and RuntimeProfileRevision.
A runtime session pins one immutable ResolvedProfileManifest and one BinaryRevision.
Domain and application layers never know provider config paths, HOME/XDG/CODEX_HOME layouts, or provider DTOs.
The orchestrator supplies opaque profile and credential references; AR resolves and materializes them.
Profile revision identity uses canonical semantic source identity, precedence, content hashes, and materializer version; it excludes mtime and absolute host paths.
Immutable profile files, mutable provider state, credentials, shared caches, and binary installations are separate resources with separate lifecycles.
Mutable provider state is not shared between independent runtime instances; shared credential use does not imply shared state.
Each provider and BinaryRevision materializes its own filesystem and environment layout behind a narrow application port.
Deterministic modes never launch a provider against writable user source config; providers receive a private materialization.
Config parsing uses provider-native introspection or a real format parser; regex JSONC parsing is forbidden.
Source scanning fails closed on unreadable, changing, unsupported, or truncated input and reports typed diagnostics.

Ambiguous extension IDs are resolved before provider launch by a deterministic declared layer order; if the source adapter cannot suppress losing copies safely, materialization requires an explicit winner or fails closed.
ACP is a preferred provider-facing adapter, not the AR domain model or lifecycle authority.
ACP v1 and v2 adapters are versioned separately; v2 is negotiated and feature-flagged until stable and conformant.
Profile preparation is staged, idempotent, content-addressed, and atomically published; provider execution never observes a partially prepared revision.
Provider processes never perform concurrent writes to one mutable state root unless a provider-specific serialized lane explicitly owns it.
Plugins, hooks, MCP servers, and executable skill assets are executable capabilities, not passive profile fields; activation requires explicit trust, grants, sandboxing, and audit.
Extension discovery, materialization, and activation are separate observable states; listing an extension does not prove it executed or was blocked.
Every external process started by a profile has bounded startup and operation deadlines, cancellation cleanup, and typed per-extension failure evidence.
Relative profile resources retain an explicit semantic base and are rebased during materialization instead of embedding host absolute paths in revision identity.
A provider materialization directory is a disposable derivative; the authoritative revision is a manifest plus verified content-addressed artifacts.
A durable runtime-session reference or materialization lease prevents garbage collection of its pinned profile revision and artifacts.
Missing or corrupt materialization is rebuilt from the same revision artifacts; missing authoritative artifacts produce PROFILE_REVISION_UNAVAILABLE and never fall back to ambient or latest config.
AR receives generic ordered profile bindings and never interprets orchestrator business scopes such as team, teammate, task, or board.

Profile composition can request behavior and executable resources but cannot grant capabilities; activation is bounded by separately revisioned grants, runtime policy, workspace trust, and BinaryRevision support.

An active RuntimeSession pins its immutable RuntimeProfileRevision. Ordinary preference or binary availability drift affects automatic capture for a future session and never interrupts the active session.
Admin-managed and AR runtime policy are represented by a renewable and revocable AuthorityPolicyBinding, never copied into RuntimeProfileRevision or its artifacts.

A provider may keep one execution generation across an authority revision only when hot enforcement is proven for that BinaryRevision; unknown, unavailable, or restart-scoped enforcement fails closed and may require a successor generation.

A profile revision consists of an ArtifactClosure plus explicit ExternalDependencyBindings. PATH executables, absolute files, packages, and shell semantics never become reproducible merely because the config bytes were captured.

Provider ACLs classify credential-bearing fields before persistence. Known secrets become opaque CredentialBindings; unknown secret-shaped or inline credential values fail closed and never enter profile artifacts or evidence.
AR owns the outer lifecycle and process group for provider-started hooks, plugins, and MCP servers; cancellation and timeout conformance must prove descendant cleanup.
Profile capture uses bounded stable reads and rejects symlinks, hard links, special files, source replacement, traversal outside the artifact root, and silent truncation.

openDecisions.question: Should the default onboarding mode be inherited_snapshot or an explicitly weaker ambient_live compatibility mode?
What are the exact team, agent, and session override semantics, including tombstones and intentional duplicate resolution?
Does RuntimeProfile remain a feature in agent-execution or become a bounded context after independent catalog, sharing, and policy lifecycle appears?
Which binary compatibility evidence is required before a pinned session may upgrade or roll back?
Which ProfileArtifactStore adapters ship first: local filesystem CAS and hosted object storage, or a database-backed small-artifact adapter as well?
